title: Can a Referral-Only Agent Still Attend Brokerage Training and Events?
metaDesc: Can a referral-only agent still attend brokerage training and events in Florida? Generally yes, though policies vary by brokerage; here is what to expect.
h1: Can a Referral-Only Agent Still Attend Brokerage Training and Events?
about: Whether referral-only real estate agents in Florida can still attend brokerage training sessions and events
answer: Yes, in most cases. Many brokerages welcome referral-only agents at training sessions, office meetings, and events, even though they’re not actively selling, because staying informed and connected still benefits the brokerage and the agent’s network. Exact access varies by brokerage, so it’s worth confirming which sessions are open to you.
takeaways: Referral-only status usually doesn’t cut you off from brokerage training and events; many brokerages actively welcome you.
Staying connected helps you refer clients with confidence, since you understand current market conditions and processes.
Some sessions built for active production agents may be less relevant to you, though they’re rarely off-limits.
Attending events keeps your name and face in front of the active agents you rely on for referrals.
Policies vary by brokerage, so confirm which trainings and events are open to referral agents rather than assuming.
tldr: Referral-only agents can typically still attend brokerage training sessions and events, since staying connected and informed benefits both the agent and the brokerage. Specific policies vary, so confirm access with your brokerage, but in most cases the door stays open.
body:
Does referral status limit your access to brokerage training?

Not usually. Moving to referral-only status changes how you earn (referral fees instead of full commissions), not necessarily whether you can walk into the office for a market update, a compliance refresher, or a holiday gathering. Most brokerages don’t build a wall around referral agents; they simply stop expecting you to carry an active production load.

Why would a brokerage want a referral agent at training?

A referral agent who stays current is more valuable to the brokerage, not less. You’re still sending clients into the pipeline, and understanding today’s market, forms, and process makes those referrals smoother and your conversations with clients more credible. Brokerages generally benefit from keeping referral agents informed and engaged rather than isolated.

What kinds of events are usually open to you?

Office meetings, market updates, compliance and continuing education sessions, and social or networking events are commonly open to referral agents. These are exactly the settings where staying visible matters most, since the active agents you’ll be referring clients to are in the room too.

Are there sessions built only for active agents?

Occasionally. A hands-on transaction workshop, a lead-generation bootcamp, or a tool built specifically for daily production work may be tailored to agents actively listing and closing. That doesn’t usually mean you’re barred, just that the content may be less directly useful to your day-to-day as a referral agent.

How do you find out your brokerage’s specific policy?

Ask directly. Policies on training and event access for referral agents vary from brokerage to brokerage and aren’t always written down in one place. A quick conversation with your broker or office manager will tell you exactly what’s open to you and what’s optional.

Should you make the effort to attend anyway?

Generally, yes. Even occasional attendance keeps you connected to the agents who close the deals you refer, keeps your knowledge current, and keeps your name in front of people who matter to your referral income. It costs little and tends to pay off in stronger, more confident referrals.

At Adams, Cameron & Co., the area’s largest brokerage since 1963, referral agents remain part of the office, welcome at training and events, and connected to a deep Volusia and Flagler agent network. If you’re weighing a move to referral-only status and want to know what staying involved looks like day to day, start a conversation.

Staying connected matters most if you might return. See going back to active selling after being a referral agent.

faq.q: Will I still be invited to brokerage meetings as a referral agent?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. Brokerages commonly keep referral agents on the invite list for office meetings, market updates, and events, since staying connected benefits both sides.

faq.q: Can a referral-only agent take continuing education through the brokerage?
faq.a: Often yes, though continuing education requirements and offerings depend on your brokerage and Florida’s rules. Confirm directly with your brokerage which CE options are available to you.

faq.q: Do referral agents pay to attend brokerage training and events?
faq.a: It varies. Some sessions are free as part of being with the brokerage, while others, like certain conferences or paid workshops, may carry a cost regardless of your status. Ask your brokerage what applies.

faq.q: Is attending events worth it if I’m not actively selling?
faq.a: Generally yes. It keeps you visible to the active agents who close your referred deals and keeps your market knowledge current, both of which support stronger referrals.

ctaHeading: Stay connected, even as a referral agent.
